headline: A warm, dry weekend gives way to a strong storm fed by a weak to locally moderate atmospheric river (a long plume of Pacific moisture) that is likely to bring at least an inch of rain from the coast to the mountains, possible thunderstorms, gusty winds and mountain snow Tuesday into Wednesday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Saturday stays dry and warmer than normal under high pressure, with highs in the mid to upper 70s across most of the coast and valleys, including the Carlsbad area. The low deserts reach the upper 70s to low 80s, the High Desert the low 70s, and the mountains the 50s and 60s. Saturday night stays dry.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Sunday is another dry, warm day with highs similar to Saturday before an incoming low pressure system pushes the warm high pressure south Sunday night. Moisture arriving Sunday night brings a chance of light rain, and periods of spotty light rain are possible Monday, mostly at rates of 0.15 inch per hour or less. The chance of more than half an inch of rain from Sunday night through Monday night is 15 to 30 percent, highest north of San Diego County. Inland areas turn 3 to 7 degrees cooler than normal starting Monday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Tuesday into Wednesday, a strong storm drops in from the northwest, bringing widespread moderate to heavy rain, gusty winds, mountain snow and a greater-than-usual chance of thunderstorms, ending sometime Wednesday morning or afternoon; Tuesday looks like the coolest day of the week. At least 1 inch of rain is likely from the coast to the mountains, with a 40 to 50 percent chance of more than 3 inches along the coast and valleys and 70 to 80 percent in the mountains from Tuesday morning through Thursday morning; the deserts will likely get at least half an inch, with a 40 to 50 percent chance of more than an inch in the low deserts and 60 to 70 percent in the High Desert. Gusts over 35 mph on Tuesday have a 60 to 70 percent chance near the coast and 40 to 60 percent farther inland, and with soaked soils, downed branches and toppled shallow-rooted trees are possible; snow levels start above 8,000 feet Tuesday morning and fall to around 6,500 feet Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, so prepare for flooding and snow impacts at 6,500 feet and above. After a brief dry break later Wednesday into early Thursday, the pattern stays unsettled with more chances of cool, wet weather late in the week, and temperatures stay below normal inland through Saturday.

coast: High tides keep dropping this weekend, from around 7 feet Saturday to below 7 feet Sunday, running about a foot above normal predictions. A reinforcing long-period west swell builds surf Saturday to 4 to 7 feet with sets to 8 feet on exposed west-facing beaches and near piers, highest in the morning and early afternoon, and combined with the high tide brings minor to locally moderate coastal flooding Saturday morning; a Beach Hazards Statement is in effect for the Orange and San Diego County coasts through Saturday afternoon. No hazardous boating conditions are expected through Monday, but southwest winds build Tuesday, with widespread gusts of 30 to 35 knots (about 35 to 40 mph) Tuesday morning through Wednesday morning, steep, choppy seas, a 20 to 30 percent chance of storm-force gusts Tuesday morning and afternoon, and a slight chance of thunderstorms over the water Tuesday.
watch_for: Rain totals, flooding and thunderstorm chances with the Tuesday–Wednesday storm
Gusty winds Tuesday on saturated ground, which could bring down branches and trees
Coastal flooding and high surf Saturday morning
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the dry, warm weekend and fairly confident in a significant Tuesday–Wednesday storm, but exact rain totals and snow levels are still being refined, and the weather late next week is less certain.
